name: Communicate credit decisions and negotiate conditions
summary: Once credit releases a decision, the sales side has to turn it into a deal or close it. The vendor desk tells dealers, the broker desk tells brokers and account executives tell their own customers what was approved and on what conditions, such as first and last payments, a down payment, a guarantor or a shorter term, or why the deal was declined. They negotiate changes within the approval, send appeals with new information back to credit and pricing requests to the deal desk, and release a document request when the customer accepts. Most elapsed time is spent waiting for dealers, brokers and customers who are also comparing other lenders' offers, and much desk time goes on chasing approvals that never come back.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size independent Canadian equipment lessor with vendor, broker and direct channels, an origination portal that posts decisions to dealers and brokers, and sales staff who follow up by phone and email.
baseline.notes: Decisions arrive from small-ticket and mid-ticket credit. Re-decisions after appeals are counted as new decisions.

trigger: Credit releases an approval, conditional approval, decline or withdrawal in the origination portal.
end_state: A document request is released to documentation, an appeal is sent back to credit, or the decision is closed as declined, withdrawn, lost to another lender or expired.

volume.seasonality: Follows applications: busier in spring for construction and agricultural equipment and at dealers' month and quarter ends; 2020 had a spring dip and then a rebound.

evidence.note: Process map figure, derived from the organisation file's 3,430 applications a month less fraud referrals and submissions above authority, plus about 200 re-decisions after appeals.

Lessors' inside sales staff relay decisions and coordinate documents with dealers. FTE is the author's estimate from step times and volume; about 3.6 of the 12 coordinators remain after quoting and intake.
Account managers step in only when a key dealer challenges a decline. Author estimate.
A Canadian lessor's broker desk coordinator is the liaison for brokers and their requests. FTE is the author's estimate from step times and volume.
Broker relationship managers negotiate on larger or contested broker deals. Author estimate.
The assigned sales account executive handles pricing, credit and documentation matters for the relationship. FTE is the author's estimate from step times and the direct share of decisions.

systems.name: Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation
Customer relationship management system (partner accounts, pipeline, commissions data)
Contact centre telephony and shared mailboxes
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)

steps.name: Post the decision and send the automatic notice
steps.description: When credit releases a decision, the origination portal updates the deal status that the dealer, broker or account executive sees and emails a decision letter: approved amount, term, rate tier, conditions and expiry date, or a decline with a general reason. The deal then sits in the follow-up queue of the desk that owns the channel.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: vendor deal handled by the vendor desk (conditions, declines, phone and email dealers)
clean vendor approval the dealer picks up in the portal
direct deal owned by an account executive

evidence.note: Real-time portal notification and automated approval letters are documented. Channel shares follow the organisation file (54% vendor, 32% broker, 14% direct); the 30% of vendor approvals handled by dealers in the portal is an author estimate.

steps.name: Pick up the decision and read the conditions
steps.description: A vendor desk coordinator takes the next decision from the desk queue, opens it in the origination portal and reads the approved structure, the conditions (for example first and last payments, a down payment, a guarantor or proof of insurance) or the decline reason codes. They compare it with the quote the desk gave the dealer and note anything the dealer will push back on.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Conditioned decisions with stipulations and first and last payments are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Tell the dealer the decision and explain the conditions
steps.description: The coordinator phones or emails the dealer's salesperson with the decision. For conditional approvals they explain what the customer must add and how the payment changes; for declines they give the general reason without revealing guarantors' personal credit details and say whether new information could change the answer. The contact is logged against the deal.

error.defect_description: A condition is left out or misstated, so the dealer quotes the customer the wrong terms.

control.basis: PIPEDA principle 4.5 (limiting use and disclosure) and the consent clause in the credit application: dealers and brokers receive the decision and conditions, not the guarantors' personal credit details

next.condition: file was withdrawn for missing information; dealer told

evidence.note: Declines explained to the provider and limits on disclosing personal information are documented. Decision mix (about 52% approvals or conditional approvals, 41% declines and 7% withdrawals among desk-handled vendor decisions) is the author's estimate, set so that about two thirds of all decisions are approvals as in the organisation file.

steps.name: Dealer presents the approval to the customer
steps.description: The dealer's salesperson takes the approval and its conditions to the customer, often while the customer is also weighing a bank loan or another lessor's offer. The customer agrees to the terms, asks for different terms, goes quiet or buys elsewhere.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: dealer asks for documents, often before the customer has fully decided
customer or dealer asks to change the structure
customer buys elsewhere or drops the purchase

evidence.note: An event log of loan offers shows customers take days to return offers and many never do. The 1-day mode and branch shares are author estimates for dealer deals.

steps.name: Negotiate changes within the approval
steps.description: The coordinator works out with the dealer whether the customer's request fits the approval: a different term, first and last payments instead of a down payment, a small change in equipment price or a different end-of-term option. Changes inside the approval's tolerances are agreed on the spot; anything else becomes an appeal to credit.

error.defect_description: A change outside the approval's tolerances is agreed with the dealer.

control.basis: Credit policy and delegated credit authority: sales may change the structure only within the approval's tolerances; any other change goes back to credit

evidence.note: Down payments, extra collateral, guarantors and first and last payments are the documented levers. Shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Account manager reviews a dealer's challenge to a decline
steps.description: When a dealer pushes back on a decline, the vendor account manager who owns the relationship looks at the deal, the dealer's volume and the decline reason, and decides whether to back an appeal with new information or to tell the dealer the decision stands.
outputs: appeal support or confirmation of decline

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Relationship managers intervening on key dealers' declines is common practice; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare and submit an appeal to credit
steps.description: The coordinator collects the new information the dealer offers, such as bank statements, a larger down payment, a co-signer or proof of time in business, writes a short note on what changed and resubmits the deal to credit as an appeal in the origination portal. The case leaves this process and comes back as a new decision.

error.defect_description: The appeal goes to credit without the information credit needs, so it is sent back.

control.basis: Credit policy on appeals: a decision is reconsidered only with new information, at the original approval level or higher

evidence.note: Re-decisioning a locked decision and approvals above offer amounts needing bank statements are documented; the wait to collect new information is an author estimate.

steps.name: Check the final structure and release the document request
steps.description: The coordinator checks the document request, keyed by the dealer in the portal or taken by phone, against the approval: equipment and serial numbers, price, term, payment, signer, guarantors, conditions and the approval's expiry date. They fill gaps, mark the deal ready for documents and the portal sends it to the documentation queue.

error.defect_description: Equipment, serial numbers, signer or tax province keyed wrongly in the document request.

control.basis: Credit policy: documents are drawn only against an unexpired approval (90 days) whose final structure matches the approved terms and conditions

evidence.note: The 90-day approval validity and the approval letter's legal name, signer and supporting documents are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Follow up the dealer on an open approval
steps.description: From the desk's open-approvals list, the coordinator phones or emails the dealer about approvals with no response after a few days, asks whether the customer is going ahead and reminds them of the expiry date. Approvals that are clearly lost are closed in the portal.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: approval closed unanswered or left to expire

evidence.note: Approvals stay valid for up to 90 days; the follow-up interval and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Dealer reads the approval in the portal and asks for documents
steps.description: For clean approvals the dealer's salesperson sees the decision in the dealer portal, confirms the deal with the customer and enters the document request with equipment details and signer without calling the desk.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: no request after a few days

evidence.note: Dealer portals showing status and approvals notified within hours are documented; shares and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Email the decision letter to the broker
steps.description: A broker desk coordinator opens the decision, attaches the decision letter to an email to the broker with the conditions listed plainly, or a decline with its general reason, and logs it. Brokers often have the same deal at other funders, so the coordinator asks whether the broker intends to proceed.

error.defect_description: Conditions misread or left out of the email to the broker.

control.basis: PIPEDA principle 4.5 (limiting use and disclosure) and the consent clause in the credit application: dealers and brokers receive the decision and conditions, not the guarantors' personal credit details

next.condition: file was withdrawn for missing information; broker told

evidence.note: The broker desk as liaison for brokers is documented. Decision mix for broker deals (about 68% approvals, 27% declines, 5% withdrawals) is an author estimate.

steps.name: Broker presents the approval and compares other funders' offers
steps.description: The broker takes the approval to the customer and compares it with offers from other funders it submitted the deal to. The customer accepts, asks the broker to negotiate, stops responding or takes another funder's offer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: broker asks for documents, often while still holding other funders' approvals
deal placed with another funder or dropped

evidence.note: Offer return delays are documented in a loan event log; the higher loss share for brokers, who shop deals, is an author estimate.

steps.name: Negotiate conditions, pricing or a challenged decline
steps.description: The broker relationship manager talks to the broker about what the customer wants: a lower rate, fewer conditions, a longer term or a second look at a decline. They agree changes within the approval, prepare a pricing request to the deal desk, or decide an appeal is worth sending with new information.
outputs: agreed structure, pricing request or appeal decision

error.defect_description: A concession outside the approval or rate card is promised to the broker.

control.basis: Credit policy and delegated credit authority: sales may change the structure only within the approval's tolerances; any other change goes back to credit

next.condition: rate below the card sent to the deal desk

evidence.note: Broker negotiation practice; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Present the deal desk's pricing answer to the broker
steps.description: After the deal desk prices the request, the relationship manager tells the broker the approved rate and structure or explains why the rate cannot move, and updates the deal in the portal.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Pricing authority matrix: rates below the rate card floor need deal desk and sales operations approval

next.condition: revised offer goes back to the broker
broker had already placed the deal elsewhere

evidence.note: Deal desk turnaround of hours to a few days is an author estimate.

steps.name: Chase the broker on an open approval
steps.description: The broker desk coordinator emails or phones brokers whose approvals have had no answer for a few days, asks whether the deal is proceeding and closes approvals the broker has placed elsewhere.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: approval closed unanswered or left to expire

evidence.note: Approvals stay valid for up to 90 days; the chase interval and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Assemble and submit an appeal package
steps.description: The broker desk coordinator collects the new information the broker sends, such as bank statements, interim financial statements, a down payment or an extra guarantor, checks it is complete and resubmits the deal to credit as an appeal with the relationship manager's note.

error.defect_description: The appeal goes to credit missing the information credit asked for.

control.basis: Credit policy on appeals: a decision is reconsidered only with new information, at the original approval level or higher

evidence.note: Extra financial information for larger or weaker deals and re-decisioning are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Check the broker's document request and release it
steps.description: When the broker asks for documents, the coordinator checks the request against the approval (equipment, vendor, price, signer, guarantors, conditions and expiry), fills gaps from the broker's email and releases the document request to the documentation queue.

error.defect_description: Vendor, equipment or signer details keyed wrongly from the broker's email.

control.basis: Credit policy: documents are drawn only against an unexpired approval (90 days) whose final structure matches the approved terms and conditions

evidence.note: Creating documents at the broker's request after checking the credit approval is documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Review the decision and conditions with the underwriter
steps.description: The account executive reads the decision and, for mid-ticket deals, calls the analyst to understand the conditions, such as covenants, a guarantee, a holdback or a shorter term, and what room there is to adjust them, before going back to the customer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: The account executive handles credit matters for the relationship while underwriting is separate; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Present the decision to the customer
steps.description: The account executive calls or meets the owner or finance manager, explains the approval, its conditions and the payment, or the decline and what could change it, and sends a written summary. For approvals they ask for the details needed for documents.

error.defect_description: A condition is misstated to the customer.

control.basis: PIPEDA principle 4.5 (limiting use and disclosure) and the consent clause in the credit application: dealers and brokers receive the decision and conditions, not the guarantors' personal credit details

next.condition: account executive appeals the decline with new information
file was withdrawn for missing information; customer told

evidence.note: A sales representative contacting the customer after approval is documented. Decision mix for direct deals (more conditional approvals, about 23% declines) is an author estimate.

steps.name: Customer considers the offer
steps.description: The customer reviews the approval with its accountant, compares it with its bank's terms and decides whether to proceed, asks for changes or walks away.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: customer uses another lender or defers the purchase

evidence.note: Customers taking days to respond and comparing rates and flexibility are documented; shares and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Negotiate structure and pricing
steps.description: The account executive negotiates with the customer: seasonal payments, a different residual, fewer conditions or a lower rate. They agree changes within the approval, prepare a pricing request for the deal desk or prepare an appeal to credit.
outputs: agreed structure, pricing request or appeal decision

error.defect_description: A structure outside the approval is promised to the customer.

control.basis: Credit policy and delegated credit authority: sales may change the structure only within the approval's tolerances; any other change goes back to credit

next.condition: rate below the card sent to the deal desk

evidence.note: Structure levers such as down payment and collateral are documented; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Present the deal desk's repricing
steps.description: Once the deal desk answers, the account executive takes the approved rate and structure back to the customer and updates the proposal.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Pricing authority matrix: rates below the rate card floor need deal desk and sales operations approval

evidence.note: Deal desk turnaround is an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare an appeal with new information
steps.description: The account executive gathers what could change credit's view, such as interim statements, a stronger guarantor, more down payment or added collateral, writes a short case and resubmits the deal to the underwriter as an appeal.

error.defect_description: The appeal lacks the information the underwriter needs.

control.basis: Credit policy on appeals: a decision is reconsidered only with new information, at the original approval level or higher

evidence.note: Re-decisioning is documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Confirm the final structure and submit the document request
steps.description: The account executive confirms the final equipment list, supplier, price, term, payment schedule, signer and guarantors with the customer, checks them against the approval and its expiry and submits the document request in the origination portal.

error.defect_description: Supplier, equipment or signer details wrong or incomplete in the request.

control.basis: Credit policy: documents are drawn only against an unexpired approval (90 days) whose final structure matches the approved terms and conditions

evidence.note: The 90-day approval validity is documented; times are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Dealer challenges a decline through the account manager
exceptions.description: A dealer pushes back on a decline; the vendor account manager decides whether to back an appeal, and the desk resubmits the deal to credit with new information.

exceptions.name: Approval goes unanswered and expires
exceptions.description: The dealer or broker never comes back, usually because the deal went to another lender; the desk chases once or twice and closes the approval.

exceptions.name: Rate below the rate card
exceptions.description: A broker or direct customer asks for a lower rate; the request goes to the deal desk and the revised offer goes back to the customer.

exceptions.name: Final request outside the approval
exceptions.description: The document request has a higher price, different equipment or a different signer than approved, so the desk renegotiates or appeals to credit.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from decision released to document request, appeal or closure, all outcomes
benchmarks.population: Author estimate for a Canadian independent lessor, informed by published decision-notice times, approval validity and offer return times

evidence.note: Decisions reach dealers within hours and approvals stay valid for up to 90 days; customers in a loan offer event log took 3 to 9 days on average to return offers. Declines close the same day, so the median is about a day.

benchmarks.unit: hours from application to decision notified to the dealer
benchmarks.population: US small-ticket lessors' published service levels

evidence.note: Within an hour for most decisions (GreatAmerica); 2 to 4 business hours (LEAF).

benchmarks.population: Marlin Business Services, US small-ticket lessor, 2019

evidence.note: The organisation file uses about 66% for a small-ticket independent.

benchmarks.unit: share of loan offers returned by the customer
benchmarks.population: Dutch financial institution's consumer loan offers, BPI Challenge 2017 event log

evidence.note: Different product and country; shows how many offers are never taken up.

pain_points.description: Dealers and brokers shop deals to several lenders, so many approvals are never answered and desk time goes on chasing them.

evidence.note: Large shares of unreturned offers are documented in a loan event log; the lessor-level share is an author estimate.

pain_points.description: Conditions are explained by phone and email and then re-keyed into the document request, so misunderstandings surface only when documents are drawn or audited.

evidence.note: Author assessment of email and portal hand-offs.

pain_points.description: Appeals often arrive without the new information credit needs and bounce back, adding days while competitors quote.

evidence.note: Author assessment.

pain_points.description: Waiting for deal desk pricing while the customer holds another offer loses deals.

evidence.note: Author assessment, consistent with the organisation file's description of the deal desk.

pain_points.description: Customers judge lessors on turnaround and consistency of credit decisions, so slow or unclear communication of conditions costs business.

evidence.note: CFLA customer survey factors.

sources.title: Marlin Business Services Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2019
sources.publisher: Marlin Business Services Corp. via US SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Partners get real-time notification of application approvals through a web platform and dealers have an online portal to view status; credit approvals are typically valid for up to 90 days from initial approval, after which a re-approval may be issued; every active relationship has an assigned sales account executive who handles pricing, credit, documentation, training and marketing matters; credit underwriting is managed apart from origination.

sources.title: What to expect in the GreatAmerica financing process (blog)
sources.supports: Approved applications get an automated approval letter by email; pending decisions mean more information is needed; declines are explained to the provider with as much information as the lessor can give; the approval letter confirms the legal name, desired signer and supporting documents; most decisions are communicated within an hour depending on transaction size; the provider then coordinates documents and signatures.

sources.title: Applying for financing (help centre)
sources.supports: The lessor typically notifies the customer or dealer of an approval after 2 to 4 business hours; the analyst approves, declines or pends for more information; once approved a sales representative is notified and contacts the customer, sends documents and lists any additional information needed; approvals above offer amounts may need bank statements or financial information.

sources.title: Oracle Financial Services Lending and Leasing: Lease Origination User Guide, Underwriting
sources.supports: Underwriters set an application to approved, conditioned, rejected or withdrawn; stipulations are items that must be addressed before the lease can be funded and can carry adverse action reasons; automatic decisions notify the producer; a decided application is locked and must be put into rehashing (re-decision) to change it, re-scoring when scoring-sensitive data change.

sources.title: Credit Coordinator, Bennington Financial (job posting)
sources.publisher: EQ Bank / EQB Inc. on Lever
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment lessor's coordinator monitors and routes emails and online applications to the internal broker desk, acts as liaison for brokers as primary customers, responds to their inquiries in a timely manner, works with credit and funding to meet broker service levels and creates lease documents at the broker's request after checking the credit approval; salary $42,000 to $46,000.

sources.title: Equipment financing credit guidelines (dealers and vendors)
sources.supports: For less-than-perfect credit a lessor expects a down payment or extra collateral; most tiers need a personal guaranty with minimum personal scores; larger deals may need tax returns, interim financials, personal financial statements or a debt schedule; application-only requests are often decided in 24 to 48 hours.

sources.title: Pros and cons of vendor financing for equipment purchases
sources.supports: Vendor financing is arranged at the dealership during the purchase; leasing through a vendor usually requires money at signing such as a first and last monthly payment; the lender still assesses the equipment's value and the buyer's creditworthiness.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principle 5: limiting use, disclosure, and retention
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: An organisation may use or disclose personal information only for the identified purposes for which it was collected; new purposes need new consent; staff access should be restricted and monitored.

sources.title: BPI Challenge 2017: process variability analysis over offers
sources.publisher: Eindhoven University of Technology (A. Bolt), BPI Challenge 2017
sources.supports: Event log of a Dutch financial institution's loan offers: only 54.2% of offers sent are returned by the customer; 40% of all offers are accepted, 11% refused and 49% cancelled; offers sent online only are returned in 3 days on average and offers sent by mail and online in 9 days; cancelled offers have the longest throughput, 23 days on average.

sources.title: ELFA Monthly Leasing and Finance Index, July 2019 (press release)
sources.supports: Credit approvals totalled 75.7% of decisions in July 2019 at the reporting equipment finance companies (77.0% in June); receivables over 30 days 2.0%; charge-offs 0.37%.

sources.title: Asset-based finance in Canada: the 2019-2020 year (Canadian Market Overview)
sources.supports: When choosing a leasing company, business customers value funding rates and affordability, the ability to reach someone to solve an issue and customer service, and also turnaround time, information requirements, flexibility and consistency in credit decisions.

assumptions: Channel shares follow the organisation file: 54% vendor, 32% broker and 14% direct. About 30% of vendor decisions are clean approvals that dealers act on in the portal without calling the desk.

Decision mix (about 66% approvals or conditional approvals, 29% declines, 5% withdrawals) is set so that roughly two thirds of decisions are approvals, as in the organisation file. In the simulation about 56% of cases end in a document request (about 1,830 a month, a little below the organisation file's 2,000 document packages), about 6% in an appeal (about 210 a month, close to the 6% and 4% appeal shares the credit workflows use) and about 1% send a pricing request. Dealers and brokers usually ask for documents as soon as a deal is approved, so most losses to competing lenders show up later as unsigned packages in prepare-lease-documents rather than here.

The case ends when the appeal is submitted; the re-decision comes back from credit as a new case. Pricing approvals from the deal desk return into an open case and do not start one, so their trigger share is 0.
Decision notices go to the dealer, broker or customer of the deal's channel; the produces list uses outcome 'any' for all three because the channel is not an outcome.
Non-bank lessors had no adverse action notice rule for commercial credit in Canada in 2019-2022; the control on what may be disclosed rests on PIPEDA and the consent in the credit application.
Delegated authority tolerances (for example how much the equipment price may rise without re-approval) are not modelled as numbers.

Staffing: about 2.8 of the 12 vendor desk coordinators (about 3.6 remain after quoting and intake), 1.6 of 4 broker desk coordinators, 0.65 of 7 broker relationship managers, 0.25 of 20 vendor account managers and 3.2 of 14 account executives work on this process. Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
External steps have zero touch time; dealer, broker and customer time is in wait_before_min.
